name: Docker hosts
author: Netlens
description: Shows your Docker hosts with their containers: state, health, restarts, image, compose project, the ports each container publishes, and containers that have their own address on your network (macvlan / ipvlan) matched to the devices Netlens found. Read-only: it only lists containers and networks. Docker's API gives full control of a host, so talk to it through a read-only socket proxy (see the README), never through an open Docker port.

info.title: What to add to this Docker host (docker compose)
info.text: Docker's API gives full control of a host, so never open port 2375 itself. Add this small read-only proxy to the compose file on every Docker host, change the address on the ports line to that host's own LAN address, start it, and enter http://<that address>:2375 below. It only allows GET requests for containers, networks and info; everything else is refused.
info.code:
services:
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      CONTAINERS: 1   # list and inspect containers
      NETWORKS: 1     # which network is macvlan / ipvlan
      INFO: 1         # the host's name
      IMAGES: 1       # optional: how old each container's image is
      POST: 0         # nothing that changes anything
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    ports:
      - 192.168.0.189:2375:2375   # this host's LAN address

config.label: Docker hosts
config.help: The read-only Docker socket proxy on each host (https:// works too). When the proxy runs on the Docker host itself and is reached as 127.0.0.1, fill in the host's own network address as well.

columns.label: Host's own address
columns.help: Only needed when the proxy is reached as 127.0.0.1
